title: Zeng Zi Keeps His Wife's Promise
text:
Zeng Zi was one of the most respected disciples of Confucius, known above all for his devotion to his parents and his scrupulous honesty. The philosopher Han Feizi, writing in the third century BC, preserved a story about him that Chinese children still learn.

One day Zeng Zi's wife was setting out for the market, and their small son followed her, crying to go along. To get rid of him she said: go back home, and when I return I will kill the pig for you. Pork was a rare treat.

When she came back from the market, she found Zeng Zi getting ready to catch the pig and kill it. She stopped him, saying that she had only been joking with the child.

Zeng Zi answered that one must not joke with a child in that way. A child, he said, knows nothing by himself; he learns from his parents and follows their teaching. If you deceive him now, you are teaching him to deceive. And if a mother deceives her son, the son will no longer trust his mother. That is not the way to raise a child. Then he killed the pig and cooked it for the boy.

The phrase "Zeng Zi kills the pig" became a Chinese saying for keeping one's word, especially to children.
lesson: Children learn honesty from the promises we keep, even casual ones. If we would not keep a promise, it is better not to make it.
people: Zeng Zi (Zeng Shen), his wife and son
source: Han Feizi, chapter 32 (Outer Collection of Explanations, Upper Left)
caveat: The story is told by Han Feizi about two centuries after Zeng Zi's lifetime.
